---
title: "Exploring Field Relationships"
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

```{r, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(REDCapExploreR)
```

`field_relationship_summary()` identifies upstream references and downstream
uses of a field in available REDCap metadata. It helps reviewers locate
configuration to inspect before changing a field. It does not modify a project,
evaluate expressions, or predict changes to stored values.

## Build a codebook first

A field name alone cannot establish its relationships. A codebook supplies the
field definitions, expressions, and instrument/event context needed to interpret
references. Build it once to explore several fields without repeated API calls.
Record data and credentials are not needed when using an existing codebook.

```{r live-project, eval=FALSE}
codebook <- build_codebook(
  redcap_uri = Sys.getenv("REDCAP_URI"),
  token = Sys.getenv("REDCAP_TOKEN")
)
relationships <- field_relationship_summary("weight_kg", codebook)
```

Codebooks built before complete definitions were added must be rebuilt. Existing
codebook viewing and saving still work with older objects.

## Explore the bundled example

`mock_codebook` extends the mock project's metadata with weight/BMI examples.
These extra fields are metadata only; the record-based quality and dashboard
fixtures do not contain them.

```{r offline}
relationships <- field_relationship_summary("weight_kg", mock_codebook)
relationships
relationships$downstream |>
  dplyr::select(item_name, connection, reference_chain, status_note)
```

| Item | Relationship to `weight_kg` |
| --- | --- |
| `baseline_weight_kg` | Upstream: the `@DEFAULT` action tag references weight from the baseline event. |
| `bmi` | Direct downstream calculation using weight and height. |
| `weight_review` | Indirect downstream reference: its branching logic uses BMI. |
| `visit_summary` | Pipes and embeds weight in its field label, and pipes weight again in its field note. |
| `starting_weight` | References weight in an `@IF` condition and an `@DEFAULT` value. |
| `weight_at_entry` | Uses a current-event smart variable in its default; interpretation requires event context. |
| `custom_record_label` | Project setting that pipes weight. |
| `diagnostic_example` | Clearly marked diagnostic example: contains ordinary piping, a deliberately unsupported action tag, and a reference to missing `retired_weight`. |

Use exact dictionary field names, including a checkbox's parent name. Labels
and exported checkbox columns such as `symptoms___fever` are not field names.

## Read upstream and downstream correctly

Upstream means fields referenced by the selected field. Downstream means fields
or settings that reference it. A direct connection is one reference step;
indirect connections follow several steps. Arrows point from the referenced field
toward the referencing item. An upstream chain is displayed from the selected
field back toward its inputs, with arrows pointing in the reverse direction.

Each chain labels its steps, for example:

`weight_kg -[Calculation]-> bmi -[Branching logic]-> weight_review`

A chain identifies configuration to review. It does not establish that values
or behavior will change. Piping a value into a field label does not change that
field's stored value, and branching logic controls display rather than calculating
an answer. Likewise, a default initializes a field; it does not establish ongoing
synchronization with its source.

Traversal operates at field level. It does not establish a continuous runtime
path through particular events, arms, or repeating instances. One deterministic
shortest chain is shown per item; alternative reference occurrences remain in
`references`. Cycles terminate without repeatedly listing the same item.
These connections are metadata references, not foreign keys, joins, cardinalities,
or guarantees of referential integrity.

## Find the configuration to inspect

| R element / viewer section | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `field` / Field | Complete selected definition, annotations, and structural context. |
| `upstream` / Upstream | Inventory of fields used directly or indirectly, with labelled chains. |
| `downstream` / Downstream | Inventory of fields and settings that reference this field, with labelled chains. |
| `summary` / Summary | Human explanations grouped by item, metadata location, expression, and interpretation. |
| `references` / References | Individual occurrences with original expressions and reference tokens. |
| `issues` / Interpretation issues | Related interpretation limits with their location, expression, and reason. This viewer section appears when issues exist. |
| `coverage` / Coverage | Project-wide source availability, other interpretation limits, and exclusions. |

```{r summary}
relationships$summary |>
  dplyr::select(dependent_name, metadata_column, expression, occurrence_count, explanation)
```

Repeated references within an expression increase `occurrence_count`; they do
not create additional related fields. References in different metadata locations
or distinct expressions remain separate Summary rows. Field labels and notes
are separate configuration to inspect, even when both pipe the same value.

The viewer uses REDCap terms such as Branching logic, Piping, Field embedding,
and Default value (`@DEFAULT`). It keeps item inventories short. Complete related
field definitions, qualifiers, character offsets, and report-local occurrence IDs
remain available in the R output. `path` contains occurrence IDs and `field_path`
contains item names; `reference_chain` gives a readable, typed chain. These IDs
are local to a report, not permanent identifiers for audit comparisons.

```{r viewer, eval=FALSE}
view_field_relationship_summary(relationships)
save_field_relationship_summary(relationships, "weight-relationships.html")
```

References initially shows every returned occurrence. Filters apply only when
you choose them. Saved HTML includes local dependencies for offline use.

## Interpret matching and issues

`relationship` describes the reference's purpose. `action_tag` retains a specific
tag when present. `field_matched` means the field name exists in the dictionary.
It does not validate the REDCap configuration.

`resolution` records qualifier/syntax interpretation:

- `resolved`: the field and supported qualifiers were identified; the expression
  was not evaluated or fully validated.
- `context_dependent`: the field is known, but event or instance selection needs
  context, or an explicit instrument-event mapping is unavailable.
- `unresolved`: a field or qualifier could not be interpreted, or a checked
  configuration constraint failed.
- `unclassified`: candidate syntax or action-tag behavior is not interpreted.

Known field references remain linked even when qualifiers need interpretation.
Unknown fields and unsupported annotation candidates do not create traversable
links. They are retained as evidence and interpretation issues. `status_note`
contains the specific reason and is empty when no interpretation limit was found.
That empty note does not certify a valid REDCap expression.

`traversal_role` is independent of interpretation: `upstream`, `downstream`,
`both` for references within both traversed regions of a cycle, or `self` for a
self-reference. `both` does not assert a direct reciprocal pair.

Related issues are always available without project-wide diagnostics:

```{r issues}
relationships$issues |>
  dplyr::select(dependent_name, metadata_column, expression, status_note)
```

For example, the missing `retired_weight` reference is in a related field's note,
but is not part of a known reference chain to `weight_kg`. Its evidence is in
`issues`; adding unrelated inputs to References would blur that table's scope.
Issues describe interpretation limits, not a count of invalid REDCap settings.

## Review a proposed change

Start with direct upstream/downstream uses and inspect their Summary locations.
Then review indirect chains and interpretation issues. Changing a name, a choice
code, a label, or a value can have different consequences:

| Proposed change | Configuration to inspect |
| --- | --- |
| Rename or remove a field | References containing its field name, including calculations, branching logic, action tags, piping, and embedding. |
| Change codes or field type | Logic and calculations expecting the current representation; checkbox choice references and piping modifiers. |
| Change labels | Piping that displays labels, including choice labels, rather than raw values. |
| Change data values | Calculations and branching logic that read those values; default values need separate consideration of when they are applied. |

These are review prompts, not predictions. The package does not establish whether
stored calculations have been recalculated, whether conditions will be true for
particular records, or whether a change is safe to deploy.

## Understand inspection scope

Coverage counts are **project-wide**, not counts of relationships for the selected
field. Source rows group available locations, nonblank expressions, and reference
occurrences by metadata source. Other-project interpretation limits are disclosed
in aggregate. Source counts overlap with interpretation-limit counts and must
not be added together as an issue total. Related issue details live in `issues`.

Supported sources include branching logic, calculated fields, field annotations,
field labels and notes, section headers, choice labels, and the custom record
label. Supported action-tag interpretation includes `@DEFAULT`, `@CALCTEXT`,
`@CALCDATE`, and conditions and recognized branches within `@IF`. Quoted ordinary
formula literals are ignored. Ambiguous quoted references in calculation action
tags are conservatively unclassified.

The extractor recognizes explicit events and numeric instances, common dynamic
event/instance selectors, checkbox choices, and piping modifiers including
`:checked:value` and `:unchecked:value`. It flags cross-instrument embedding,
but does not validate every embedding, instrument-page, action-tag, or expression
constraint. REDCap versions can support syntax outside this parser's scope.

Alerts, automated survey invitations, survey queues, report filters, data quality
rules, external modules/scripts, and other settings outside retained metadata are
not inspected. An empty result does not establish the absence of external uses.

Request a full project inventory only when needed:

```{r diagnostics}
detailed <- field_relationship_summary("weight_kg", mock_codebook, include_diagnostics = TRUE)
detailed$diagnostics |>
  dplyr::count(row_kind, status)
```

This adds `diagnostics` and an optional Diagnostics viewer section without changing
related issue details or compact Coverage. It includes blank and unavailable
locations and can be large.
